 TOR 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles will start Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Barnes is back after a four-game absence, but it won’t be Murray-Boyles who heads to the bench. Jakob Poeltl will be replaced in the starting lineup, which is good news for those who have CMB rostered. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes (adductor) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Barnes has missed the last four games with a left groin strain, but went through part of practice on Saturday. He’s questionable to return Sunday against the Knicks. If Barnes remains out, Collin Murray-Boyles should continue starting for the Raptors. 
 Collin Murray-Boyles 
 TOR 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Collin Murray-Boyles finished with 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), four assists, one steal, five blocks and one three-pointer against the 76ers on Thursday. 
 Murray-Boyles is starting to pick up the production after a rough start to the season. He set a new season high for blocks in this game and has at least one swat in three straight games. CMB hasn’t popped like many managers were hoping for, but he is beginning to produce high-level value in multiple categories. Entering the starting unit has helped, which will hopefully allow him to keep it going as the season continues, even if he eventually moves back to the bench.

 #4 
 Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the 76ers. 
 Barnes will miss a fourth straight game while dealing with a left groin strain. That should mean another start for Collin Murray-Boyles, who has averaged 13.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.0 “stocks” across his last four starts. 
 Kawhi Leonard 
 TOR 
 Forward 
 #2 
 Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Kawhi Leonard (knee) is doing individual work and progressing well. 
 Leonard has not appeared in a game since October 23, and it was announced on Tuesday that he would be re-evaluated in one week. Rajakovic’s update is positive, but Leonard remains limited to individual work. When available, Collin Murray-Boyles has been part of the starting lineup in recent games.

 Murray-Boyles is back after missing Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies. His return likely bumps Kyle Anderson, who played 16 minutes on Monday, to the bench.

 Murray-Boyles did not play in Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies, leading to Kyle Anderson’s first start of the season. Anderson played only 16 minutes and isn’t worth streaming if CMB remains out.

 Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Barnes will miss his third consecutive game with an adductor injury. Collin Murray-Boyles could move into the starting lineup in Barnes’ absence. 
 Jakob Poeltl 
 TOR 
 Center 
 #19 
 Jakob Poeltl supplied 18 points (9-of-12 FGs, 4-of-9 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks over 31 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Let’s face it, Poeltl isn’t an exciting fantasy proposition at this stage of his career. However, he keeps producing like an upper-echelon center, when healthy. The 31-year-old big man has been on a roll over the past week, averaging 15 points, eight boards and nearly two blocks over his last three games. He’ll face a much stiffer test against the Celtics and their Neemias Queta and Mitchell Robinson tandem in the middle on Wednesday.
